open_points.subject: A01 rule 4 equal-submission behavior
open_points.text: `canonical_values` Owns A01 rules 1 and 4: canonical JSON (RFC 8785) and the SHA-256 identities of content records and values computed from it
open_points.question: Which module owns the record-dependent parts of A01 rule 4—finding an existing record, returning it unchanged, preserving its first author and time, and not making an equal contract or flow version current—given that `canonical_values` may know neither `store` nor the domain modules and exposes no capability for those decisions?
options: `canonical_values` owns only identity/equality; each domain module owns equal-submission behavior
`store` owns equal-submission behavior for every content-derived record
`canonical_values` remains the owner and receives additional record-aware dependencies and capabilities
open_points.default_guess: Treat `canonical_values` as owning only identity/equality and the relevant domain module as owning the equal-submission behavior.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile M22 creation
open_points.text: Two have several, on purpose: StoredValue M21 and value bytes are written by whichever module produces or receives the value ...; NodeExecution M23 is written by `effects` ... and by `runs` ...
open_points.question: Who owns creation of SpooledFile records, since later text says both `runs` and `effects` write files and set their classes, but the exhaustive statement of record types with several writing modules names only StoredValue and NodeExecution?
options: SpooledFile is a third intentionally multi-writer record, produced by `runs` and `effects` through `store`
`store` alone creates SpooledFile records and callers only supply bytes and classification facts
`runs` exclusively owns SpooledFile records, including files produced by operation nodes
open_points.default_guess: Treat SpooledFile as a third intentionally multi-writer record, with `runs` and `effects` invoking `store.spool_file`.

open_points.subject: surface dependency on store_persistence
open_points.text: `surface`, which may know every module ... Every read and write of a row goes through one typed record port, `StoreRepository` ... its one implementation is `SqliteStoreRepository`, owned by `store_persistence` ... only `store` calls it
open_points.question: Does “every module” permit `surface` to know `store_persistence` and its public repository capabilities, or is `store_persistence` private to `store` and excluded from `surface`'s dependency set?
options: `surface` knows every module except the private `store_persistence` companion
`surface` may depend on `store_persistence` types but may never call them
`surface` may know and call all public capabilities, including `store_persistence`
open_points.default_guess: Exclude `store_persistence` from `surface`'s dependencies and expose persistence only through `store`.
